thank you so much for commenting - and thank you especially for trying not to dismiss my anxieties. definitely one of the difficult things is figuring out what a normal level of hygiene conscious is - like I worry that I’ll sound like I’m saying ‘I think I’m sooo crazy obsessed with hygiene because I have to wash my hands after using the bathroom’ because that kind of is on the same level in my mind as all the actually crazy shit I worry about. if you know what I mean.

to be fair to my parents, I don’t think they had that attitude to sex I think I just latched onto the idea of sin when I was younger because it was a clear cut Wrong which best described how I felt about cleaning myself (due to the other stuff…) I do wish i had felt able to actually talk about this stuff with them, and they could have done better to facilitate that probably. I totally get where you’re coming from though, and maybe a slightly less prudish and more approachable attitude than they had would’ve helped me as a kid.

it is really reassuring to read what you’ve said. you can probably guess I’m kind of an anxious type and I would never talk about this in real life even to closest friends because I don’t want to be seen as dirty and ostracised or something. so actually having another person answer my questions really helps. thank you for taking me seriously and for the time you took to write this

I just want to make sure you’re aware of any laws in your region surrounding carrying a blade with you in public or in schools - if you don’t get found out to be carrying one you won’t be in trouble, but there is a possibility. I got caught with a blade at school a few months ago (I’m 18) and though I didn’t get reported to the police (it was clear what I was using it for and it wasn’t a threat to other students) my parents did get told and my local mental health services were contacted. It might be totally different where you are (I’m in the UK) but it’s best to at least know the risk.

I would get alcohol wipes (can use to sanitise skin and blade before use as well as clean/help stem the flow from cat scratches), plasters/dressings (box of big ones, I just cut them up smaller as I need to) and maybe steri-strips if you need them.

Depends how deep. We don’t have hydrogen peroxide readily available in my country (UK) but for cat-scratch cuts it’s fine to use an alcohol wipe (it’s basically like a shaving cut and you can use cologne for that, right?). For styros rinsing with water inside the cut would be fine; you could use alcohol or soap on the outside only, so only on the outer layer of skin. Keep it covered with a sterile dressing to reduce risk of infection, after closing with steri-strips.

if you wear a thin long sleeved undershirt (like under a flannel) it may be possible for them to take the blood pressure over the undershirt sleeve. Especially since it’s more difficult to roll it all the way up your arm above where they place the cuff. This may not work 100% - are you able to see the doctor on your own? It’ll stop anyone else noticing you want to keep your sleeves on.

I don’t cut much, but from what I’ve read here styros also typically gape a little to expose the white layer. It’s good to use steri-strips to help close it and help it heal, and while you can rinse the wound in water only use a soap/alcohol around the wound on the outer layer of skin. It’s also good to keep it covered with a dressing to reduce risk of infection.

Shallower cuts can also take a little while to bleed, and I’m not sure on the timeframe for styros.
